# Draft:Maki Fujiwara

----
Maki Fujiwara (1941—1999) was a Japanese actress, artist, cartoonist, and writer. She first gained notoriety in the 1960s as an actress in Tokyo's underground Angura theater scene.
The wife of influential alternative manga artist Yoshiharu Tsuge, Fujiwara began herself drawing and writing in the 1970s and 1980s. Her best-known work is the autobiographical My Picture Diary, published in Japan in 1982 and first translated in English by Ryan Holmberg in 2023.
Life and work
Maki Fujiwara was born in 1941 in Osaka as Fujiwara Makiko. She grew up in extreme poverty, largely due to the effects of World War II, and her father was killed in combat. In 1945, American firebombs destroyed her family's house and belongings. Maki, her mother, and her siblings evacuated to a village in the mountains, Kamo-machi, where they lived in a room in a community center.
For high school, Maki returned to Osaka; after graduation, she began acting with the Kansai Art Theater, a company working in the Shingeki mode. In 1966, she moved to Tokyo and worked with Budō no kai and Henshin before joining the Situation Theater, an avant-garde troupe run by Jūrō Kara.
She later worked with Makoto Satō in the Freedom Theater. She met Tsuge in 1969 and began living and traveling with him, moving away from her acting career. In 1975, the couple had a son, Shōsuke, named after the peasant leader in Kamui (1964 manga).  Maki was diagnosed with uterine cancer in 1977, receiving treatment over the next few years.
Maki began drawing in the mid-1970s and wanted to record her family life. A small publisher saw her work and proposed publishing it, with the first edition published in Japan in October 1982. In My Picture Diary, Maki writes about her home life taking care of the house, her child, and her husband, who was often ailing with anxiety and depression. She details her complex relationship with Tsuge and his occasional outbursts, with each page containing a text entry and a drawn vignette. Booklist gave the English translation a starred review.
Maki died in 1999 of stomach cancer at 57 years old.
